chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Talha, raising it (to the Prophet), saying:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Angels are upon three parts – one part has two wings, and one part has three wings, and one part has four wings.'
ai.seo_question: How many wings do angels have according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the physical diversity of angels, categorizing them into three groups based on their wing count: two, three, or four. While some scholars interpret these numbers literally, others view them as indicative of varying degrees of spiritual capacity and speed in executing divine commands. This classification underscores the hierarchical nature of the celestial realm within Shia cosmology.
